newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK Crown prosecuter takes over Co-Op case.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK Crown prosecuter takes over Co-Op case.

text.p: Britain's state prosecutor on Tuesday took over the Co-Operative Wholesale Society's (CWS) private criminal prosecution against entrepreneur Andrew Regan and his associates David Lyons and Allan Green.

CWS said in a statement that the Crown Prosecution Service, which prosecutes criminal cases on behalf of the State, has asked police to make further investigations into the case brought by the supermarkets-to-funeral parlours group against Regan, who in April failed in a 1.2 billion pound ($2 billion) bid attempt for the CWS.

The CWS case against Regan, along with his business partner David Lyons, centred around confidential CWS documents and alleged "aiding, abetting, counselling or procuring the theft and for handling stolen property".
Allan Green, a former senior executive with CWS, is accused by his former employer of theft of confidential documents.
Regan and Lyons have said they intend to defend the case vigorously.

CWS said it had invited the prosecutor's office to take on the case and the CPS confirmed that it had done so, adding that this did not guarantee that the case would be prosecuted. It will be if the CPS feels there is sufficient evidence and that it would be in the public interest.
"The seriousness of this situation has been recognised by the appropriate authorities who have now taken responsibility for the matter," CWS said in a statement.
The abortive bid for CWS by Regan's caused great controversy earlier this year and was blocked when the High Court barred the use of the documents in the bid and Regan's financial backers withdrew.

CWS has received substantial out of court financial settlements of civil proceedings from Regan, Lyons and Green as well as from their investment banking advisers Hambros and their lawyers Travers Smith Braithwaite.
A further hearing in the criminal proceedings is set for July 3, the CPS spokeswoman said. It is likely that this will be adjourned pending the police investigation.
